claim.claim-text: 1. A sample-indexed nucleic acid library preparation, comprising: a plurality of dual-indexed nucleic acid fragments generated from a sample, wherein each individual nucleic acid fragment of the nucleic acid fragments comprises a 5' adapter sequence, a 5' index sequence, a 3' adapter sequence, and a 3' index sequence, wherein a first plurality of different 5' index sequences selected from a first set of 5' index sequences associated with the sample and a first plurality of different 3' index sequences selected from a second set of 3' index sequences associated with the sample are represented in the dual-indexed nucleic acid fragments and wherein the first plurality of different 5' index sequences and the first plurality of different 3' index sequences are distinguishable from one another.

2. The library preparation of claim 1, further comprising: a plurality of dual-indexed nucleic acid fragments from a second sample, wherein the dual-indexed nucleic acid fragments from the second sample are modified with the 5' adapter sequence and the 3' adapter sequence and wherein a second plurality of different 5' index sequences and a second plurality of different 3' index sequences are represented in the dual-indexed nucleic acid fragments from the second sample and wherein the second plurality of different 5' index sequences and the second plurality of different 3' index sequences are distinguishable from one another and from the first plurality of different 5' index sequences and the first plurality of different 3' index sequences.
3. The library preparation of claim 2, wherein:

each index sequence of the first set of 5' index sequences and the first set of 3' index sequences is present in the first plurality of nucleic acid fragments and at a ratio relative to the other index sequences in the first set of 5' index sequences and the first set of 3' index sequences between 0.9 to 1.1, optionally wherein each index sequence of the first set of 5' index sequences and the first set of 3' index sequences is present in the first plurality of nucleic acid fragments at approximately equal proportions; and/or each index sequence of the second set of 5' index sequences and the second set of 3' index sequences is present in the second plurality of nucleic acid fragments and at a ratio relative to the other index sequences in the second set of 5' index sequences and the second set of 3' index sequences between 0.9 to 1.1, optionally wherein each index sequence of the second set of 5' index sequences and the second set of 3' index sequences is present in the second plurality of nucleic acid fragments at approximately equal proportions.
4. The library preparation of claim 2 or claim 3, wherein:

the 5' index sequences from the first set of 5' index sequences are only located 5' of a target sequence and are not located 3' of the target sequence in the first plurality of nucleic acid fragments, and the 3' index sequences from the first set of 3' index sequences are only located 3' of the target sequence and are not located 5' of the target sequence in the first plurality of nucleic acid fragments; and/or the 5' index sequences from the second set of 5' index sequences are only located 5' of a target sequence and are not located 3' of the target sequence in the second plurality of nucleic acid fragments, and the 3' index sequences from the second set of 3' index sequences are only located 3' of the target sequence and are not located 5' of the target sequence in the second plurality of nucleic acid fragments.
5. The library preparation of any one of claims 2 to 4, wherein:

at least two fragments of the first plurality of nucleic acid fragments have the same combination of 5' and 3' index sequences; and/or at least two fragments of the second plurality of nucleic acid fragments have the same combination of 5' and 3' index sequences.

6. The library preparation of any one of claims 2 to 5, wherein the first set of 5' index sequences and the first set of 3' index sequences are associated with the first sample and not the second sample, and wherein the second set of 5' index sequences and the second set of 3' index sequences are associated with the second sample and not the first sample, optionally wherein the first sample and the second sample are nucleic acid samples from different individuals.

7. The library preparation of any one of claims 2 to 6, wherein the 5' index sequence and the 3' index sequence are positioned between the 5' adapter sequence and the 3' adapter sequence, optionally wherein the 5' adapter sequence is a p5 adapter sequence and/or wherein the 3' adapter sequence is a p7 adapter sequence.
8. The library preparation of claim 7, wherein the 5' index sequence is located between the 5' adapter sequence and a sequencing primer on each nucleic acid fragment.

9. The library preparation of claim 7 or claim 8, wherein the 5' adaptor sequence is the same sequence in each nucleic acid fragment of the first plurality and the second plurality and/or wherein the 3' adaptor sequence is the same sequence in each nucleic acid fragment of the first plurality and the second plurality.
10. The library preparation of any one of claims 2 to 9, wherein the 5' index sequence is 5-10 bases in length and the 3' index sequence is 5-10 bases in length.

11. The library preparation of any one of claims 2 to 10, wherein the first set of 5' index sequences comprises at least four different index sequences and the first set of 3' index sequences comprises at least four different index sequences and/or wherein the second set of 5' index sequences comprises at least four different index sequences and the second set of 3' index sequences comprises at least four different index sequences.
12. A sample-indexed nucleic acid library preparation, comprising:

a first nucleic acid library prepared from a first sample, wherein the first nucleic acid library comprises a first plurality of nucleic acid fragments, wherein each nucleic acid fragment of the first plurality comprises at least two different index sequences selected from a first set of index sequences; and a second nucleic acid library prepared from a second sample, wherein the second nucleic acid library comprises a plurality of nucleic acid fragments, wherein each nucleic acid fragment of the second plurality comprises at least two different index sequences selected from a second set of index sequences that are distinguishable from the first set of index sequences, wherein the index sequences are arranged on individual nucleic acid fragments of the first plurality and second plurality such that a first index sequence of the index sequences is located 5' of a target sequence and a second index sequence of the index sequences is located 3' of the target sequence, and wherein:

(i) the first plurality of nucleic acid fragments comprises individual nucleic acid fragments having different combinations of the two different index sequences from the first set of index sequences relative to other individual nucleic acid fragments within the first plurality of nucleic acid fragments; and/or (ii) the second plurality of nucleic acid fragments comprises individual nucleic acid fragments having different combinations of the two different index sequences from the second set of index sequences relative to other individual nucleic acid fragments within the second plurality of nucleic acid fragments.
13. A sequencing substrate comprising a plurality of immobilized capture molecules hybridized to respective nucleic acid fragments of a library preparation according to any one preceding claim.
